newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition says not admitting breakaway group.
newsitem.headline: India coalition says not admitting breakaway group.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition decided on Thursday not to admit a breakaway faction of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, the alliance's spokesman said.

"The United Front has decided not to give membership to the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)," spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters. "Regarding ministers of RJD, no view has been taken," he said, referring to three ministers of the group in Gujral's council of ministers.
Reddy was speaking after a select panel of the alliance's leaders held a four-hour meeting to discuss deep divisions over ethics and ideology, widely viewed as a test of its unity.

One alliance partner, the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), wanted Gujral to expel the RJD from the coalition because its leader, Laloo Prasad Yadav, has refused to resign as the chief minister of Bihar state after federal police indicted him in a $280 million embezzlement scandal. Yadav says he is innocent.

Another partner, the regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party, had threatened to pull out of the government, saying the communists were overstepping their limits by interfering in the affairs of Gujral's party. Four of Gujral's ministers belong to the DMK.
Yadav broke away from the prime minister's party on July 5 and set up the RJD, citing differences over an election for the Janata Dal's top post.
